evidence: web/panel.html, web/dashboard.html and web/debug.html fetch nothing off-origin: every request is a relative /api/... path, and the only image source is a data: URI built in lib/state/companions.js:279 (`image: `data:image/png;base64,...``). A grep for http(s):// across the three files returns zero hits, so there is no third-party origin to preconnect to.

No self-hosted font is used anywhere. Every stack is local/system: web/panel.html:24 `font: 15px/1.5 Charter, "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif` and web/dashboard.html:13-15 `--display: "Avenir Next Condensed"...`, `--mono: ui-monospace...`. There is no @font-face rule in any of the three files, so no preload or font-display is owed.

View state that a user would expect to survive a refresh or a shared link is held only in JavaScript variables. web/dashboard.html:174 `let expanded = null;` plus web/dashboard.html:309 `expanded = expanded === tr.dataset.id ? null : tr.dataset.id;` means the expanded gap-detail row is unlinkable and lost on refresh; web/panel.html:1285-1289 `el.onclick = () => { ... startReader(s.asin); }` switches the book being read with no URL record, so a refresh silently reverts to the default book.
fix: Sync the dashboard's expanded row to `?gap=<id>` (read it on load with `new URLSearchParams(location.search)` and write it with `history.replaceState`), and put the panel's selected ASIN in `?asin=` so startReader() can restore it after a reload.

evidence: There is no router and no navigate/router.push call in any of the three files. Real navigation uses real anchors: web/dashboard.html:163 `Debug console · Raw stats` and web/debug.html:123 `Back to the dashboard`. The `

None of the stateful overlays can be reached by URL. web/panel.html:434 `<div class="reader-menu-overlay" id="reader-menu-overlay" role="dialog">` opens only through `openReaderMenu()` (web/panel.html:1700), web/panel.html:439 `<div class="star-cal-overlay" ... role="dialog">` only through `_openStarCal()` (web/panel.html:1813), and the calendar's month/day selection lives in the plain object `const _cal = { view: 'month', key: null, stars: [] }` at web/panel.html:1812. Same for the dashboard's expanded row (web/dashboard.html:174).
fix: Drive the overlays and the calendar month/view from the query string (for example `?overlay=stars&month=2026-08&calview=day`), reading it on load and writing it with history.replaceState when the state changes, so any of these surfaces can be linked to directly.

evidence: Two irreversible actions fire on a single click with no confirmation and no undo. web/dashboard.html:339 `$('standdownday').addEventListener('click', async () => { await post('/api/standdown', { day: true }); refresh(); });` sets `stoodDownForDay = true` for the rest of the calendar day (lib/engine.js:263-266) and nothing in the UI or the API can clear it before the day rolls over (lib/engine.js:94-97). web/panel.html:1579-1584 `$('reader-retry').addEventListener('click', ... fetch('/api/reading/retry', ...))` calls `retryBook()` -> `revive({ clearFirst: true })` (lib/reader.js:903-907), which the panel's own copy at web/panel.html:993 describes as "throws away what Amazon has stored here".
fix: Put a confirmation step in front of both: for "Off for today" either confirm ("Stop delivering for the rest of today?") or add a visible "Resume today" control backed by a new POST /api/standdown/clear that resets stoodDownForDay; for "Try again" confirm that the reader's stored Amazon registration will be discarded before POSTing /api/reading/retry.

evidence: There is no touch-facing surface to apply touch-action to. The daemon binds loopback only (lib/server.js:573 `server.listen(config.port, '127.0.0.1', resolve);`) and the panel is a fixed-size macOS window (config/interstice.config.default.json `"panel": { "width": 440, "height": 620 ... }`), so no page in web/ is ever reached from a touch device.

Same absent referent as UX-TOUCH-001: no touch-facing project surface exists. The three stylesheets in web/ carry no -webkit-tap-highlight-color declaration, but the pages are served only to 127.0.0.1 (lib/server.js:573) and rendered in a desktop macOS panel window, where the tap highlight never appears.

The reading menu overlay is scrollable and does not contain its overscroll, while every other scrollable surface in the same file does. web/panel.html:130-134: `body.immersive .reader-menu-overlay.open { display: flex; ... position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 29; padding: 16px; overflow-y: auto; background: ... }` has no `overscroll-behavior`, unlike web/panel.html:59 (#companions), :94 (main), :156 (.forfeit-note), :172 (.star-cal-overlay) and :246/:260 (.reader .text/.over), which all set `overscroll-behavior: contain`.
fix: Add `overscroll-behavior: contain;` to the `body.immersive .reader-menu-overlay.open` rule at web/panel.html:130-134 so scrolling the menu does not chain to the page behind it.

evidence: No drag implementation exists in the target. There is no dragstart/dragover/drop listener, no pointerdown-driven move handler and no draggable attribute in web/panel.html, web/dashboard.html or web/debug.html; the only pointer handlers are single clicks (for example web/panel.html:1613 `$('reader-frame').addEventListener('click', ...)`).

There is no autoFocus attribute anywhere in web/. The only automatic focus on an input is web/panel.html:518 `if (name === 'queue_prompt' && fromServer) $('box').focus();`, which targets the single primary input of that view (`<textarea id="box">` at web/panel.html:461, the only field on the surface) and fires only when the daemon itself delivers that rung. The remaining focus() calls are modal-open focus moves to the close control (web/panel.html:1712, 1815), which is correct dialog behavior.

No notched or home-indicator surface exists for env(safe-area-inset-*) to apply to. The pages are served only on loopback (lib/server.js:573 `server.listen(config.port, '127.0.0.1', resolve);`) and the panel runs as a fixed 440x620 macOS window (config/interstice.config.default.json `panel`), so the sticky header at web/panel.html:31-36 and the footer at web/panel.html:294-297 never meet a device inset.

Every surface that can outgrow its container scrolls inside its own box rather than pushing the page sideways: web/dashboard.html:86 `.tablewrap { overflow-x: auto; ... }` wraps the only wide element (the gaps table, web/dashboard.html:303), web/debug.html:46 `pre { ... overflow-x: auto; ... }` wraps the JSON dump, and the panel's body cannot scroll at all (web/panel.html:25 `display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden;`). The narrow-width grids degrade cleanly (web/dashboard.html:65 `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(168px, 1fr))`, web/dashboard.html:80 `grid-template-columns: 104px 1fr 54px`). Checked by static inspection; the running app was not driven at 360/768/1440px.

Layout is CSS throughout: flex on the panel shell (web/panel.html:25, 32-33, 94-96) and grid for the ease row and calendar (web/panel.html:214 `.ease { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); }`, :179 `.cal-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(7, 1fr); }`, web/dashboard.html:65, :80). The two measurement calls are not layout: web/panel.html:802-805 `readerBox()` reads getBoundingClientRect only to tell the remote headless renderer what pixel size to lay a Kindle page out at, and web/panel.html:551-553 sizes a cross-document iframe from its own scrollHeight, which CSS cannot do.

All three pages ship a full dark palette but never declare color-scheme, so native scrollbars, form controls and the canvas behind the page stay in light mode. web/panel.html:13-19 `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --ground: #0E1116; ... } }` with no `color-scheme` property anywhere in the file; identical omission at web/dashboard.html:17-24 and web/debug.html:16-22. A grep for `color-scheme` in web/ matches only the three media queries.
fix: Add `color-scheme: light dark;` to the bare `:root` rule in each of web/panel.html:8, web/dashboard.html:8 and web/debug.html:8 so the UA follows the theme for scrollbars, the textarea at web/panel.html:286 and the number input at web/debug.html:93.

evidence: No page declares a theme-color. The heads carry only charset, viewport and title (web/panel.html:4-6, web/dashboard.html:4-6, web/debug.html:4-6), while the page background changes between themes (--ground is #F1F3F5 light / #0E1116 dark at web/panel.html:9 and :15).
fix: Add per-theme meta tags to each head, matching the --ground token: `<meta name="theme-color" content="#F1F3F5" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)">` and `<meta name="theme-color" content="#0E1116" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">` (use #EEF0F2/#0E1116 for dashboard.html and debug.html).

evidence: There is no native <select> in the target. A grep for `<select` across web/panel.html, web/dashboard.html and web/debug.html returns zero hits; the only form controls are the textarea at web/panel.html:286-291, the checkboxes at web/panel.html:1323 and the number input at web/debug.html:93, all of which already set explicit background and color (web/panel.html:288, web/debug.html:43).

The dark flip breaks button-label contrast and several token pairs fall under AA in both themes. web/panel.html:223 `button.act.primary { background: var(--accent); color: #fff; }` and web/dashboard.html:62 `button.primary { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; }` sit on --accent #2440E8 in light (7.06:1, passes) but on --accent #8296FF in dark (web/panel.html:16, web/dashboard.html:21), where white text measures 2.71:1, below the 4.5:1 body-text bar. Also failing: --faint #8B96A3 on --ground/--raised/--sunk in dashboard light (2.63/3.00/2.44:1, used at web/dashboard.html:92 `tr.synthetic td { color: var(--faint); }`, :94 `.p-mute`, :99 `.excluded`) and --faint #6C7784 in dashboard dark (4.15/3.83/4.02:1); --warn #A8620F on --ground in panel light (4.27:1, used at web/panel.html:63 `#companions .top .label { color: var(--warn); }` and :276 `.signin .label`); --warn #9A6A12 in dashboard light (4.14:1 on --ground, 3.84:1 on --sunk); and --rule as the sole boundary of every button and card (web/panel.html:219, web/dashboard.html:57) at 1.19-1.47:1 against its backgrounds, under the 3:1 interface-component bar in both themes.
fix: Darken --accent in the dark palettes (or set `color: var(--ground)` on .primary buttons in dark) so the primary button label reaches 4.5:1; raise --faint to about #6E7885 (light) / #8A96A4 (dark) and --warn to about #8A5100 (panel light) / #7E5606 (dashboard light); and give interactive borders a token at 3:1 or better rather than reusing --rule. Then re-measure every pair, hover, disabled and pill colour included, on both flips.

evidence: User-visible times are assembled by hand instead of formatted. web/panel.html:1785-1790 `_wallClock` does `const m = String(iso).match(/T(\d{2}):(\d{2})/); return m ? `${m[1]}:${m[2]}` : String(iso);` and its output is shown to the user at web/panel.html:1801 ("Block forfeited at 14:32") and web/panel.html:1844-1845 ("began 09:05 · ended 09:30"). Raw ISO day keys are also printed as dates: web/panel.html:1844 ``A block earned on ${star.day}`` and :1874 ``Stars in ${key}``. web/panel.html:1268 `new Date(d.staleSince).toLocaleString()` and web/dashboard.html:329 `new Date().toLocaleTimeString()` are called with no locale or options argument. There is no `Intl.` reference anywhere in web/.
fix: Replace _wallClock with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' }).format(new Date(iso))`, format star.day and the calendar title with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { dateStyle: 'long' })` / `{ month: 'long', year: 'numeric' }`, and pass explicit locale plus options to the toLocaleString calls at web/panel.html:1268 and web/dashboard.html:329.

evidence: Percentages and durations are built by string math rather than Intl.NumberFormat. web/dashboard.html:171 `const pct = (x) => (x * 100).toFixed(1) + '%';` feeds the false-positive and stand-down figures (web/dashboard.html:210, 248, 252); web/dashboard.html:238 concatenates `width:${(n / max) * 100}%`; the percent signs in web/panel.html:1231 `return b.percent + '% · position ' + ...` and web/panel.html:1277 `(s.percent === null ? '' : s.percent + '%')` are likewise hand-appended. No `Intl.NumberFormat` exists in web/.
fix: Define `const pctFmt = new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 });` and use `pctFmt.format(x)` at web/dashboard.html:171 and for the panel's percent strings; keep the raw arithmetic only for the CSS width value at web/dashboard.html:238.

evidence: No locale is ever selected from a country code, a geo IP lookup or a CDN header. The only network calls in web/ are same-origin /api/... fetches (for example web/panel.html:570, web/dashboard.html:317), the server binds loopback (lib/server.js:573), and the date/number calls that do exist fall through to the runtime's own locale (web/panel.html:1268 `toLocaleString()`, web/dashboard.html:172 `toLocaleString([], {...})`), which is the navigator-derived default.

Product names and CLI commands are rendered as ordinary translatable text. web/dashboard.html:188 `'No events in 24 hours. Detection may be broken. Run interstice doctor.'` and web/dashboard.html:332 `'Daemon not reachable. Start it with interstice start.'` mark up commands with and no translate="no"; the same is true of the brand and identifier strings at web/panel.html:322 `Interstice`, web/panel.html:576 `'Anki is not answering'`, web/panel.html:619-622 ("Reconnect to Anki", "AnkiConnect") and web/panel.html:1232 `' · ASIN ' + b.asin`. A grep for `translate=` in web/ returns zero hits.
fix: Wrap the command and identifier spans in `translate="no"` (for example `interstice doctor`, `` for the ASIN) and add `translate="no"` to the brand span at web/panel.html:322 and the product names in the Anki and Amazon copy.

evidence: The only element carrying a value attribute is uncontrolled, which is the rule's stated alternative: web/debug.html:93 `<input type="number" id="secs" value="30" min="1" max="1800">` sets a default and is read on demand at web/debug.html:174 `Number($('secs').value)`, never re-written from state. The checkboxes at web/panel.html:1323 pair their `checked` attribute with a real change handler (web/panel.html:1395 `box.addEventListener('change', ...)`), and there is no React in the repo.

There is no server-rendered markup to mismatch. lib/server.js:554-555 serves the HTML files verbatim (`return serveFile(res, path.join(ROOT, 'web', 'debug.html'), 'text/html');`, same pattern for panel.html and dashboard.html) and every date is produced client-side after load (web/panel.html:1364 `Date.now()`, web/dashboard.html:329 `new Date()`), so no hydration boundary exists.

No suppressHydrationWarning appears anywhere in the repo; there is no React and no hydration step, only static HTML served by lib/server.js:554-555 and driven by inline vanilla scripts (web/panel.html:488, web/dashboard.html:167, web/debug.html:126).

Three interactive surfaces in the panel have no hover style at all. web/panel.html:42-49 defines `.rungs button`, `.rungs button[aria-current="true"]` and `.rungs button:focus-visible` but no `:hover`, so the four rung tabs (web/panel.html:324-327) give no pointer feedback. web/panel.html:186-189 defines `.cal-star` and `.cal-star:focus-visible` with no `:hover`, so every star button in the calendar is inert under the pointer. web/panel.html:317 `a { color: var(--accent); }` and web/dashboard.html:104 give links no hover treatment either, unlike the buttons at web/panel.html:221 `button.act:hover` and web/dashboard.html:59.
fix: Add `.rungs button:hover { color: var(--ink); border-color: var(--rule); }` at web/panel.html:49, `.cal-star:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, var(--raised)); }` at web/panel.html:189, and an `a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }` rule in both files.

evidence: Hover lowers the label contrast on the dashboard and debug buttons instead of raising it. web/dashboard.html:59 `button:hover { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }` (identical at web/debug.html:40) moves the label from --ink to --accent: measured against --ground that is 15.88:1 -> 6.18:1 in light and 15.38:1 -> 6.98:1 in dark, so the resting state is the more prominent one for the text even though the border gains contrast (1.28:1 -> 6.18:1). The disabled rule at web/dashboard.html:61 `button[disabled] { opacity: .4; }` drops the same label to roughly 2.6:1 in light.
fix: Keep the label at --ink on hover and signal the state with the border and a background wash instead (`button:hover { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent-soft); }`), so every interactive state is at least as contrasty as rest.

evidence: No user-visible string uses we, our or I. The copy addresses the reader in the second person or the imperative throughout: web/panel.html:461 `placeholder="What do you want to hand off next?"`, :1088-1090 "A Chrome window opens on Amazon's sign-in page and closes itself as soon as you are in", web/dashboard.html:270 "Submit a prompt in Cowork or Claude Code and let it run past the threshold." A grep for first-person pronouns inside quoted strings matches only the day-of-week array entry 'We' at web/panel.html:1879.

No space-constrained label spells out "and". The rung tabs are single words (web/panel.html:324-327 `Cards`, `Book`, `Queue`, `To-do`), the table headers are single words (web/dashboard.html:304 `<th>When</th><th>Surface</th>...<th>Ended</th>`), and the buttons name one action each (web/dashboard.html:128-130, web/debug.html:80-84). The only "and"s sit in full prose sentences, for example web/dashboard.html:162 "Reads timestamps and structure from agent transcripts".

No em dash, en dash or spaced-hyphen-as-dash appears in any user-visible string in the three pages. A Unicode grep over web/panel.html, web/dashboard.html and web/debug.html matches U+2014 only twice, both inside JavaScript comments (web/panel.html:1811 `// ... Nothing is stubbed (3.9) — an empty history renders an honest empty calendar.` and web/panel.html:1834 `// offline/file:// — honest empty, never stubbed`), and every ` - ` hit is arithmetic (for example web/dashboard.html:229 `b[1] - a[1]`). The copy uses the middle dot instead, as at web/panel.html:1231 `b.percent + '% · position '`.

Every page ships the same permissive viewport tag with no zoom lock: web/panel.html:5, web/dashboard.html:5 and web/debug.html:5 all read `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">`. There is no user-scalable or maximum-scale token anywhere in web/.

The to-do rung renders an unbounded array with no virtualization. web/panel.html:1334 `'<ul class="todo" data-open>' + open.map((it) => todoItemHtml(it)).join('')` (and :1338 for the done half) maps every item the API returned; lib/state/notes.js caps the number of lists (`.slice(0, maxLists)` at lib/state/notes.js:253) but never caps items per list, so a long Notes checklist is rendered in full into a 440x620 panel. Each item also gets its own change listener at web/panel.html:1394-1395.
fix: Cap or window the item render: slice to the first N open items with a "show the rest" control, or add an items cap alongside maxLists in lib/state/notes.js and paginate the remainder.

evidence: There is no autoFocus attribute in web/. The one automatic input focus, web/panel.html:518 `if (name === 'queue_prompt' && fromServer) $('box').focus();`, is justified by the surface: the queue view exists to receive typing, its only field is the textarea at web/panel.html:461, and the focus fires only when the daemon delivers that rung. The re-focus after saving (web/panel.html:1444) and the dialog focus moves (web/panel.html:1712 `document.getElementById('reader-menu-close').focus();`, :1815) are focus management, not autoFocus.

Two overlays can outgrow the viewport with a close control that scrolls away. web/panel.html:130-134 `body.immersive .reader-menu-overlay.open { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 29; padding: 16px; overflow-y: auto; ... }` holds everything the immersive view displaces (web/panel.html:1697 `const READER_MENU_DISPLACED = ['rungs', 'book-title-wrap', 'book-bar-wrap', 'reader-pager', 'reader-note', 'book-actions', 'companions', 'footer-bar'];`) inside a 620px-tall panel, and its close button (web/panel.html:435 `<button class="act om-close" id="reader-menu-close" ...>Close ×</button>`) is a plain first child with no sticky positioning. The setup banner has the same shape: web/panel.html:55-60 bounds #companions with `max-height: 40vh; overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain;`, but its Recheck and Dismiss buttons sit in a non-sticky `.top` row (web/panel.html:62-71, markup at :332-337) above content that grows with the error lists written at web/panel.html:1529-1530. The star calendar at web/panel.html:175-176 shows the correct pattern (`.star-cal-overlay header { position: sticky; top: -16px; ... }`).
fix: Pin both close affordances: wrap the reader menu's close button in a `position: sticky; top: 0` header with the overlay's own background (and add `overscroll-behavior: contain`), and add `position: sticky; top: 0; background: var(--raised); z-index: 1;` to `#companions .top` at web/panel.html:62 so Dismiss stays reachable at any scroll position.

evidence: Several pending branches render a static string with no spinner, skeleton or shimmer, in a file that has all three available (web/panel.html:303-312). web/panel.html:1581-1582 `b.disabled = true; b.textContent = 'Reopening';` is the only feedback while POST /api/reading/retry is in flight, and no say() call accompanies it. web/panel.html:1521-1522 `const wasLabel = button.textContent; button.textContent = 'working';` is static for the whole companion fix round trip. web/debug.html:160 `$('out').textContent = 'capturing the menu bar twice, a second apart…';` covers a multi-second capture with plain text, and web/dashboard.html:126 `reading daemon status…` is the initial pre-fetch state.
fix: Use the existing indicators: set `b.innerHTML = ' Reopening'` at web/panel.html:1582 and the same for the companion fix button at web/panel.html:1522, swap web/debug.html:160 for the spinner markup already defined at web/debug.html:51, and give web/dashboard.html:126 the spinner span until the first refresh() resolves.

evidence: Two user actions can produce no visible signal at all. web/panel.html:1901-1902 `document.getElementById('cal-prev')?.addEventListener('click', () => { if (_cal.view === 'month' && _cal.key) _renderStarCal('month', _shiftMonth(_cal.key, -1), _cal.stars); });` (and cal-next on :1902) does nothing when `_cal.key` is null, which is exactly the state the calendar opens in when no star exists yet: web/panel.html:1823-1827 `_thisMonth()` returns null, web/panel.html:1829 `if (!yyyyMM) { _renderStarCal('month', null, []); return; }` sets key to null, so both month arrows are permanently dead with no disabled state and no message. web/panel.html:1435-1436 `const text = $('box').value.trim(); if (!text) return;` makes the Save button a silent no-op on an empty prompt box, with no say() and no field-level error.
fix: Give both an outcome: disable cal-prev/cal-next (or seed `_cal.key` with the current month) whenever `_cal.key` is null, and replace the bare `return` at web/panel.html:1436 with `say('nothing to save yet');` plus focus on the textarea.

evidence: There is no multi-step form or wizard in the target. The only input surfaces are single-step: the one-textarea queue view (web/panel.html:456-464), the checkbox list (web/panel.html:467-473) and the single number field on the debug console (web/debug.html:91-96). The four rungs at web/panel.html:324-327 are independent activities, not ordered steps, and each is reachable directly.

The project ships a documented debug surface. web/debug.html is served at /debug (lib/server.js:554-555 `if (url.pathname === '/debug' || url.pathname === '/debug/') { return serveFile(res, path.join(ROOT, 'web', 'debug.html'), 'text/html'); }`) and drives states the happy path cannot reach in a session: open/advance/stand-down/end a gap (web/debug.html:79-85), a timed run (web/debug.html:91-96) and forced companion verdicts (web/debug.html:107-113). It is documented in README.md:322-327 under "## Debug route" and reachable from the dashboard footer (web/dashboard.html:163 `Debug console`), with the CLI equivalent at README.md:319 `interstice simulate `.

Every asserted result is shown with its working. The deck choice prints its arithmetic (web/panel.html:599-602 `d.metric.meanReps + ... + ' per due card, the lowest of ' + d.metric.decksWithDue + ' decks with anything due · ' + d.metric.due + ' due here of ' + d.totalDue + ' overall'`); the companion check attaches the menu-bar strip it read as proof (web/panel.html:1488-1489 `''`); the transcription never passes itself off as the book (web/panel.html:912-917 "Read from the page Amazon drew · some of this page read poorly"); read-ahead is checkable (web/panel.html:1026-1028 "2 ready"); forfeits name cause and wall-clock time (web/panel.html:1800-1802); and the dashboard exposes the raw decision trace per gap (web/dashboard.html:156 "Click a row for the raw decisions behind it.", rendered at :283-289) plus a link to the raw stats (web/dashboard.html:163). Nothing secret is exposed: the footer states "Reads timestamps and structure from agent transcripts, never message content" (web/dashboard.html:162).

The panel ticks an elapsed-wait counter at the user during the prompt flow. web/panel.html:1760-1763 `function _ensureTimer() { if (_latTimer) return; _latTimer = setInterval(() => _renderLatency(Date.now()), 1000); }` drives the chip written at web/panel.html:1746-1749 `return m > 0 ? `waited ${m}:${String(s % 60).padStart(2, '0')}` : `waited 0:${String(s).padStart(2, '0')}`;`, shown over the reading view from submit until completion (web/panel.html:1767). The dashboard does the same at 3-second cadence: web/dashboard.html:191 `${fmtSec(h.gap.elapsed)} elapsed` re-rendered by `setInterval(refresh, 3000)` at web/dashboard.html:342.
fix: Drop the 1-second interval and compute the wait once at the milestone: on `complete(sessionId)` (web/panel.html:1768) show a single "waited 2:14" alongside the existing arrival note, and while in flight show only the arrival-pending indicator with no ticking number.

evidence: A failed or in-flight fetch renders as a real zero result in two places. web/panel.html:1834 `} catch { _renderStarCal('month', yyyyMM, []); } // offline/file:// — honest empty, never stubbed` sends an unreachable /api/stars/month straight to the empty branch, which prints "No stars earned this month yet." (web/panel.html:1892) even though nothing was ever loaded. web/panel.html:1426-1432 `loadQueued` has no loading branch at all: `$('queued').innerHTML = (d.queued || []).slice(-6).reverse().map(...)` leaves the list rendering as empty markup both before the fetch settles and when the queue is genuinely empty, and its catch (`catch { /* daemon gone */ }`) leaves that same empty list on screen after a failure.
fix: Split both into three branches. Give the calendar a loading state (skeleton cells) before the fetch, an explicit "Could not load your stars" failure branch in the catch at web/panel.html:1834, and the empty copy only on a successful empty response; add a shimmer placeholder to #queued before the fetch at web/panel.html:1428 and an explicit "The daemon is not answering" line in its catch.

evidence: User-visible text uses unexpanded acronyms. web/panel.html:1232 `' of ' + b.end.toLocaleString() + ' · ASIN ' + b.asin` prints ASIN with no expansion, as does the shelf line it feeds (web/panel.html:1270). web/panel.html:1085 `'password, emailed code, or scan the QR with your phone'` uses QR unexpanded and is a fragment rather than a sentence. Amazon's refusal is also relayed twice in one breath at web/panel.html:990-994, where "Please try to open this book from the library again" and the real cause ("what Amazon refused was this reader's registration as a device") both appear, the answer arriving only after the quote.
fix: Expand on first use and lead with the answer: "Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) B01ABC" or drop the label to a tooltip; "scan the Quick Response (QR) code with your phone"; and reorder web/panel.html:990-994 to open with "Amazon refused this reader's registration as a device." before quoting its message.
